# mklaunchd

> A macOS CLI that generates launchd plists, validates them, and prints the launchctl commands to load them. The macOS equivalent of mkunit for systemd.

mklaunchd is a developer tool for personal automation on macOS. It writes a valid launchd plist for any binary or script, validates it against common mistakes (KeepAlive on a scheduled job, relative paths, UserName on a user agent), creates the log directory, and prints the exact `launchctl bootstrap`, `print`, `list`, and `bootout` commands needed to manage the resulting service. It does not wrap, replace, or hide launchctl — once the plist is on disk you are back in standard Apple tooling.

It supports three scopes: user agents, system agents, and launch daemons, each written to the appropriate plist directory with the matching launchd domain. It supports plugins via the git convention — any executable named `mklaunchd-<command>` on PATH becomes a subcommand. macOS 13+, Swift, MIT licensed, Homebrew distributed.

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/uradical/mklaunchd/blob/main/README.md): Install instructions, quick-start usage, examples.
- [Man page source](https://github.com/uradical/mklaunchd/blob/main/docs/mklaunchd.1.md): Complete CLI reference covering every subcommand and flag.
- [Plugin authoring guide](https://github.com/uradical/mklaunchd/blob/main/docs/plugins.md): How to extend mklaunchd with custom subcommands; environment contract; examples in Swift, Go, and shell.

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/uradical/mklaunchd): Swift source, issue tracker.
- [Homebrew formula](https://github.com/uradical/mklaunchd/blob/main/Formula/mklaunchd.rb): `brew tap uradical/mklaunchd && brew install mklaunchd`.
